name: Freightcar America, Inc.
business_overview: FreightCar America, Inc., through its subsidiaries, designs, manufactures, and sells railcars and railcar components for the transportation of bulk commodities and containerized freight products in the United States and Mexico. The company operates through two segments: Manufacturing and Aftermarket. It offers a range of railcars, including boxcars, covered and open-top hopper cars, intermodal and non-intermodal flat cars, mill gondola cars, coil steel cars, coal cars, dynastack series, steel products, boxcars, aluminum coal cars, stainless steel and hybrid stainless steel cars, and other railcar types, as well as other supplies for all railcar types, and provides aftermarket services including safety training, railcar inspections, and preventative maintenance. The company also sells used railcars; rebuilds, converts, and leases railcars; and sells forged, cast, and fabricated parts for various railcars. It serves shippers, railroads, and financial institutions. FreightCar America, Inc. was founded in 1901 and is headquartered in Chicago, Illinois.

narrative.text:
**Business & market dynamics:** The narrative has pivoted sharply from a mid-cycle reset to a commercial inflection point. Earlier in the year, a guidance cut signaled softening demand, but heavy second-quarter orders across all core segments and a landmark multi-year contract through 2028 have restored multi-year revenue visibility. This surge points to a stronger equipment replacement cycle and broad-based customer confidence, indicating demand is recovering faster and more durably than the earlier contraction suggested.

**Management strategy and execution:** Leadership absorbed a credibility hit from the guidance cut but quickly stabilized the story by reaffirming full-year targets and steering the business toward a disciplined, backlog-driven model. The team secured repeat orders from key customers, advanced tank-car retrofit and aftermarket expansion programs, and leveraged flexible manufacturing. The multi-year deal demonstrates success in converting commercial momentum into durable backlog, rebuilding some market confidence in execution.
